title: Gaining the Wealth of Inner Happiness | How-to-Live Talk With Meditation

# Gaining the Wealth of Inner Happiness
### Speaker • Brother Padmananda, Self-Realization Fellowship

## Introduction
Welcome, devotees and friends. Today we gather to explore the most important pursuit of human life: the quest for true, lasting happiness. Paramahansa Yogananda often taught that we are all, consciously or unconsciously, seeking bliss. We look for it in relationships, possessions, and achievements, yet we find that these outer treasures are fleeting. True wealth—the kingdom of God within—is the only bank account that cannot be depleted.

## The Nature of Lasting Happiness
Why is it that the happiness derived from worldly success feels like trying to hold water in our hands? It slips away because it is based on duality. Anything that has a beginning must have an end. But the soul is eternal. When we anchor our consciousness in the Divine, we touch the source of all joy.

**Story • The King and the Beggar**

Story: A powerful king once asked a great sage, "Why am I unhappy despite having all the wealth of the kingdom?" The sage replied, "O King, you are like a man who walks over a treasure chest buried beneath his floorboards, all the while begging for coins at the gates of his own palace. You seek outside what is already your own nature. Your wealth is the Spirit within you, but you have mistaken the reflection of joy for the light itself."

## Practical Application: The How-to-Live Principles
To cultivate this inner wealth, we must practice the "How-to-Live" principles taught by our Guru. It begins with the discipline of the mind. 

1. **Right Attitude:** Do not allow your happiness to be contingent upon circumstances. Practice equanimity.
2. **Right Activity:** Perform your duties with the consciousness of God, offering the fruits of your labor to the Divine.
3. **Right Meditation:** Without Kriya Yoga and deep, daily meditation, we remain at the mercy of our restless senses.

## The Role of Meditation
Meditation is not merely a practice; it is the process of reversing the flow of energy. Ordinarily, our life force flows outward through the senses to interact with the world. In meditation, we gather that energy and draw it inward to the spiritual eye. This is where the wealth of inner happiness resides—the 'Joy-that-is-ever-new.'

## Conclusion: Your Divine Heritage
Do not settle for the meager crumbs of fleeting excitement when you are invited to the banquet of God’s bliss. Practice, persist, and pray. The Guru is always with you, guiding you back to the home of your soul.

*"Divine Mother, Thou art the source of all happiness. Help me to find Thee in the silence of my own heart."*
